proposals.title: Fix mutable-global and evidence gaps to land CanonicalEncoder
proposals.why_now: All FASE-1 production logic is gated behind a committed CanonicalEncoder. After 9 cumulative review attempts across TASK-0004/0005/0006, the two remaining blockers are precisely identified and narrow: (1) Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and Number.NaN are read from mutable globals during array traversal instead of being captured as module-level constants at initialization — a post-import accessor can execute user code during encoding, violating ADR-009 zero-user-code-execution requirement; (2) npm run compile and npm run boundary evidence is absent as independently captured command output and cannot be treated as independently verified. These are the only two FAIL criteria from TASK-0006-review-03. Nothing else is blocked by the encoder specification itself.

proposals.title: Implement nominal types and integer arithmetic in packages/core
proposals.why_now: Once CanonicalEncoder is committed, the next FASE-1 dependency chain requires the full core package: branded types for Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, and Tick with constructors that enforce the ADR-003 invariants. Without these types, the ledger, price generator, and order execution cannot be correctly typed, and the compiler cannot enforce that a Tick is never added to a Money or that a division always declares its rounding mode. Every other FASE-1 component depends on this layer.

proposals.title: Write ADR for hash function and implement positional RNG
proposals.why_now: The positional RNG is a DEFINIR item that must be resolved by ADR before implementation (§19). It is required by the price generator, macro events, and bot policy — all FASE-1 components. The spec recommends SplitMix64 over FNV-1a as a starting point and requires the function to be specified bit-by-bit. Without the ADR written first, any implementation is unacceptable per the spec's own protocol. After nominal types are committed, this is the next unblocked FASE-1 dependency.

proposals.title: Implement multi-commodity double-entry ledger
proposals.why_now: The ledger is the core of the economic engine and is required for every FASE-1 acceptance criterion involving money or asset movement (INV-04 through INV-07). It depends only on core types and has no dependency on the price generator or RNG, so it can proceed in parallel with or immediately after IDEA-003.

proposals.title: Write octave parameter ADR and implement price generator (2 assets, 2 layers)
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires a price generator with at least two noise layers and two assets. The octave count, periods, and amplitudes are a DEFINIR item that must be resolved by ADR before implementation. With core types, RNG, and the ledger committed, this is the last major foundational component needed to close FASE-1 and satisfy INV-02 and INV-03 with real data. Deferring it further pushes all downstream phases.

repository_assessment.current_state: Infrastructure complete: CI pipeline (4 blocking gates), strict TypeScript config, ESLint determinism rules enforcing §13 prohibitions, dependency boundary checker enforcing §14.5 graph, and their tests. All 8 packages, 4 desktop sub-apps, and 3 tool packages are empty stubs (export {} only). Zero production logic committed. No ADRs written. The project has spent 26 cycles blocked on a single task: ADR-009 CanonicalEncoder in packages/core. All 9 review iterations across TASK-0004/0005/0006 have been rejected, with the same two FAIL criteria in the final review: (1) Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER read from mutable global during traversal instead of captured at module initialization, and (2) npm run compile and npm run boundary evidence absent as independently captured command output.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: The CanonicalEncoder (ADR-009) has not been committed after 9 review attempts. Until it is committed, no StateHash can exist, which blocks INV-01 and INV-22, and by extension all downstream FASE-1 acceptance criteria. The specific remaining fixes are narrow and precisely identified in TASK-0006-review-03: capture Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and Number.NaN as module-level constants before any traversal code, add a monkeypatch regression test proving zero accessor invocations, and capture compile and boundary command output independently.

warnings: The benchmark has consumed approximately 26 cycles with zero committed production logic beyond infrastructure scaffolding. FASE-1 has at least eight additional major deliverables (core types, RNG, ledger, price generator, orders, tick loop, save/replay CLI, Electron installer with minimum UI). At the current rate of one blocked task consuming all cycles, FASE-1 completion within the 30-day window is at serious risk. Once the encoder is unblocked, subsequent tasks should be scoped to deliver one coherent FASE-1 component at a time rather than attempting large multi-component implementations.

TASK-0004 through TASK-0006 failed REVIEW-001 (mutable global read) and REVIEW-002 (missing compile/boundary evidence) across all 9 attempts. The next implementation of the CanonicalEncoder must explicitly demonstrate: (a) every reference to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and Number.NaN replaced with a module-level const captured before any export, and (b) npm run compile and npm run boundary run on the exact committed state with full stdout/stderr and exit codes included as independent evidence — not summarized by the implementer.

Zero ADRs exist in docs/decisions/ despite multiple DEFINIR items that the spec requires to be resolved by ADR before their dependent implementations can begin: the hash function (ADR-002), the encoding specification (ADR-009), octave parameters for the price generator (§5.1), the technical enforcement of division rounding modes (ADR-004), IMPACT_WINDOW (ADR-007), and BOT_DECISION_PERIOD (§5.3). Each DEFINIR item must have its ADR written before the implementation it governs is started. The ADR backlog will compound as more FASE-1 components come online.
